name: maket-http-connector
title: HTTP connector for Maket structured workspaces

framing.intent: Maket is a visual document tool for AI agents. Its structured workspaces list items that come from a data source, behind the ItemSource interface: cursor listing, search, read, create, write, delete, identity declared in the schema, revision to detect conflicts. Today, plugging in a REST API takes code written for that API. The outcome wanted: an HTTP connector that implements ItemSource on top of a REST API described by configuration, so that a workspace reads and writes the items of that API.

actors.name: The owner
actors.description: Chooses the APIs to plug in, provides the base URL and the name of the environment variable that holds the secret, reads the resulting workspaces.

actors.name: The agent composing workspaces
actors.description: Declares a structured workspace plugged into the connector, then lists, searches, reads and edits the items through Maket's MCP tools.

actors.name: The external API
actors.description: Third-party REST service that holds the items. It is authoritative on their content and their revision.

in: List items by cursor, with the API's own pagination and search parameters.
Read an item by its identity.
Write an item with PUT and the If-Match header carrying the known revision; a 412 answer is returned to the agent as a stale revision.
Identity and revision of the items declared in the workspace schema: identity field, source of the revision (ETag or response field).
Authentication by a secret read from an environment variable of which only the name appears in the configuration.
Read-only workspace when the API offers no write: the connector then refuses every write.
Optionally, detection of changes made outside Maket, by webhook or by periodic polling.
out: Interactive OAuth authentication and token refresh.
APIs that are not REST: GraphQL, SOAP, gRPC.
Business transformation of the data beyond the declarative field mapping.
Automatic merging of conflicts: a conflict is reported to the agent, never resolved in its place.

constraints.statement: The connector implements the existing ItemSource interface without changing it.
No secret is written into the schema, the configuration or the documents: only the name of the environment variable.
A write without a known revision is refused: no blind overwrite.
An HTTP error is returned to the agent with its status and the API's message; a write is never retried silently.

assumptions.statement: The targeted APIs return JSON and expose a stable identity per item.
Maket's ItemSource interface already covers cursor, search and revision, so the connector has nothing to add to it.

questions.question: Are creation (POST) and deletion (DELETE) part of the first version?
questions.recommendation: Yes: POST with the identity returned by the API, DELETE with If-Match. They complete ItemSource and cost little once PUT is in place.
questions.answer: Yes: creation (POST) and deletion (DELETE) are part of the first version, as recommended.

questions.question: How is the mapping from the API's JSON response to the item's fields declared?
questions.recommendation: By JSON pointers in the workspace schema: path of the list, of the next cursor, of the identity, of the revision. No transformation language.
questions.answer: By JSON pointers declared in the workspace schema: path of the list, of the next cursor, of the identity and of the revision. No transformation language.

questions.question: To follow changes made outside Maket, do we start with the webhook or with periodic polling?
questions.recommendation: Periodic polling first: it does not require Maket to be reachable from outside. The webhook comes next.
questions.answer: Periodic polling first, because it does not require Maket to be reachable from outside; the webhook comes next.

questions.question: Which forms of pagination does the connector accept: opaque cursor, page number, Link header?
questions.recommendation: Opaque cursor and Link header. A page number is converted into a cursor by the connector.
questions.answer: Opaque cursor and Link header; a page number is accepted but converted into a cursor by the connector, so that the workspace only sees the cursor contract.

questions.question: If the API returns neither an ETag nor a revision field, is writing still allowed?
questions.answer: No. A revision comes from an ETag sent back in If-Match, or from a version or date field declared as the revision by a pointer of the workspace schema. Without either, the write is refused with the reason "read-only source" and the workspace is read-only; no write by content comparison.

questions.question: Where does the owner configure the connector (base URL, environment variable name, JSON pointers), and how does he see the state of the source in Maket?
questions.recommendation: The configuration is a workspace definition, written by the agent through the MCP tool that creates or updates definitions, like the data schema. Maket shows in the workspace a read-only source panel: URL, variable name, reachable or not, read-only or not, date of the last refresh, and a "test the connection" button. No form to enter the pointers, and the secret is never entered in Maket.
questions.answer: The configuration stays written by the agent in the workspace definition. Maket has a "Connectors" screen that lists every source in use with its kind, the workspace using it, the base URL, the environment variable name, reachable or not, read-only or not, the date of the last refresh, the last error, and a "test the connection" button. In the workspace, a connector status indicator is visible without opening the screen. No secret is entered in Maket.

glossary.definition: An entry of a structured workspace, read or written through ItemSource.
Value provided by the API that changes with every modification of an item; it is used to detect a concurrent write.
The ItemSource implementation that talks to a REST API described by configuration.

artifacts.title: Writing an item: revision, conflict and read-only
artifacts.source:
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as The agent (ACT-02)
  participant M as Maket: structured workspace
  participant C as HTTP connector
  participant API as The external API (ACT-03)
  A->>M: edit item X
  M->>C: put(X, known revision)
  alt The API gives a revision (ETag or declared field)
    C->>API: PUT /items/X, If-Match: revision
    alt Revision unchanged
      API-->>C: 200, new revision
      C-->>M: item updated
      M-->>A: ok, revision N+1
    else Stale revision
      API-->>C: 412 Precondition Failed
      C-->>M: refusal "stale revision", current data read again
      M-->>A: refusal, form reloaded
    end
  else The API gives no revision (Q-05)
    C-->>M: refusal "read-only source"
    M-->>A: refusal, workspace read-only
  end

requirements.statement: The connector SHALL implement the ItemSource interface of Maket (list, get, create, put, delete, refresh) over a REST API described by the workspace configuration.
requirements.rationale: The connector replaces code written for each API by configuration; the workspace only sees the existing item source interface.
requirements.title: ItemSource over REST

requirements.statement: The connector SHALL read the base URL, the environment variable name holding the secret, and the JSON Pointer mapping (list path, next cursor path, identity path, revision path) from the workspace configuration.
requirements.rationale: The answer to Q-02 fixes the mapping from the API to the item's fields by JSON pointers, without a transformation language.
requirements.title: Workspace configuration

requirements.statement: The connector SHALL send the secret read from the configured environment variable in every request, and SHALL never write the secret into the configuration or the workspace.
requirements.rationale: No secret is written into the configuration (CON-02); only the variable name appears there.
requirements.title: Secret from an environment variable

requirements.statement: When the workspace asks for a batch of items, the connector SHALL call the list endpoint with the cursor and search parameters of the API and SHALL return items, the next opaque cursor and the total when the API gives one; a batch never exceeds 500 items.
requirements.rationale: Cursor listing is the workspace contract; the connector translates that contract to the API.
requirements.title: Cursor listing

requirements.statement: When the API paginates by page number or by a Link header, the connector SHALL convert that pagination into the opaque cursor of the workspace.
requirements.rationale: Answer to Q-04: the workspace sees a single contract, the cursor one.
requirements.title: Pagination conversion

requirements.statement: When the workspace asks for one item by its identity, the connector SHALL call the get endpoint and SHALL return the item data with its revision.
requirements.rationale: Reading by identity and the revision are needed to open and to write an item.
requirements.title: Reading an item

requirements.statement: When the workspace writes an item with a known revision, the connector SHALL send PUT with the If-Match header carrying that revision.
requirements.rationale: No write without a revision (CON-03): the known revision protects against lost updates.
requirements.title: Write with If-Match

requirements.statement: If the API answers 412 Precondition Failed to a write, then the connector SHALL refuse the write as a stale revision and SHALL return the current item data read again from the API.
requirements.rationale: A conflict is reported to the agent with the current data, never resolved in its place.
requirements.title: Stale revision (412)

requirements.statement: While the API gives neither an ETag nor a declared revision field, the connector SHALL declare the source read-only and SHALL refuse every write with the reason read_only.
requirements.rationale: Answer to Q-05: without a revision, the write is refused rather than approximate.
requirements.title: Read-only without revision

requirements.statement: When the workspace creates an item, the connector SHALL send POST and SHALL return the identity and revision assigned by the API.
requirements.rationale: Answer to Q-01: creation is part of the first version.
requirements.title: Creation with POST

requirements.statement: When the workspace deletes an item with a known revision, the connector SHALL send DELETE with the If-Match header and SHALL report 412 as a stale revision.
requirements.rationale: Answer to Q-01: deletion is part of the first version, protected like writing.
requirements.title: Deletion with If-Match

requirements.statement: While a polling interval is configured, the connector SHALL re-read the list at that interval and SHALL emit a source-changed signal when any item revision differs from the last read.
requirements.rationale: Answer to Q-03: periodic polling comes before the webhook, because it does not require Maket to be reachable.
requirements.title: Periodic polling

requirements.statement: Where the API offers a webhook, the connector MAY accept its calls and SHALL emit the same source-changed signal as polling.
requirements.rationale: Answer to Q-03: the webhook comes next, for the APIs that offer it.
requirements.title: Optional webhook

requirements.statement: If the API is unreachable or answers with a server error, then the connector SHALL report source_unreachable with the retry delay and SHALL NOT retry silently.
requirements.rationale: No silent retry (CON-04): the workspace keeps its last dated window and the agent knows why.
requirements.title: Unreachable API

requirements.statement: When a request to the API exceeds the configured timeout, the connector SHALL abort it and SHALL report source_unreachable with the timeout as retry delay.
requirements.rationale: A slow API must not freeze the workspace; the timeout is configuration, not a constant.
requirements.title: Timeout exceeded
Configuration in the definition
requirements.statement: The connector configuration (base URL, environment variable name, JSON Pointer mapping, polling interval, timeout) SHALL be part of the workspace definition written through the structured workspace definition tool, and SHALL be validated by the same check as the rest of the definition.
requirements.rationale: Answer to Q-06: the configuration is a workspace definition, so it is the agent's job, like the data schema.

requirements.title: Connectors screen
requirements.statement: The Maket application SHALL show a Connectors screen listing every data source in use with its kind, the workspace using it, the base URL, the environment variable name, whether it is reachable, whether it is read-only, the last refresh date and the last error.
requirements.rationale: Answer to Q-06: the owner must see what is plugged in and whether it works, without reading JSON.

requirements.title: Connection test
requirements.statement: When the owner asks to test a connector from the Connectors screen, the connector SHALL perform one list request with the configured secret and SHALL report reachable or the error received, without changing any item.
requirements.rationale: Immediate feedback on the configuration, with no effect on the data.

requirements.title: Status indicator in the workspace
requirements.statement: The workspace index SHALL show a connector status indicator (reachable, unreachable since a date, read-only) visible without opening the Connectors screen.
requirements.rationale: Answer to Q-06: the state of the source shows where the owner works.

requirements.title: No secret entry
requirements.statement: If any screen or tool of Maket receives a secret value for a connector, then Maket SHALL refuse it and SHALL point at the environment variable name instead.
requirements.rationale: The secret lives in the machine's environment; Maket only knows its name (CON-02).

criteria.title: A workspace plugged into a test API
given: A test REST API with 3 customers under /items
criteria.when: the agent creates a structured workspace whose source is the HTTP connector of that API
then: the 3 customers appear in the workspace index,
the workspace's MCP view returns a batch of 3 items with their identity and revision

criteria.title: Reading the configuration
given: A workspace definition with baseUrl https://api.example.com/v1, secretEnv CRM_TOKEN, the pointers /data for the list, /next for the cursor, /id for the identity, /etag for the revision
criteria.when: the connector starts
then: it reads these five values and invents no other
a definition without the identity pointer is refused by the workspace check with the name of the missing field

criteria.title: The secret is sent, never written
given: The environment variable CRM_TOKEN is s3cret and the definition holds only its name
criteria.when: the connector calls the API
then: every request carries the Authorization header with s3cret
neither the definition, nor the workspace, nor the logs contain the string s3cret

criteria.title: A batch with cursor and total
given: An API that paginates by cursor with 120 items and a total
criteria.when: the workspace asks for a first batch of 50
then: the connector returns 50 items, an opaque next cursor and the total 120
a batch asked with that cursor returns the next 50 without duplicates

criteria.title: The batch is bounded
given: An API that accepts a batch size of 1000
criteria.when: the workspace asks for a batch of 1000
then: the connector asks the API for at most 500 and returns at most 500

criteria.title: Pagination by Link header
given: An API that paginates by a Link rel=next header
criteria.when: the workspace asks for the next batch with the cursor it received
then: the connector follows the URL of the Link header
the workspace never sees the URL, only an opaque cursor

criteria.title: Reading by identity
given: An item with identity 42 and the ETag W/"7"
criteria.when: the workspace asks for item 42
then: the connector returns the item's data and the revision W/"7"

criteria.title: Write with the known revision
given: Item 42 read with the revision W/"7"
criteria.when: the workspace writes item 42 with that revision
then: the PUT /items/42 request carries If-Match: W/"7"
the API answers 200 and the connector returns the new revision

criteria.title: Revision conflict
given: Item 42 changed in the API since it was read, revision moved from W/"7" to W/"8"
criteria.when: the workspace writes item 42 with the revision W/"7"
then: the API answers 412
the connector refuses with the reason stale_revision and returns the current data with W/"8"
Maket's form reloads with that data

criteria.title: Source without revision
given: An API that returns neither an ETag nor a declared revision field
criteria.when: the workspace tries to write an item
then: the connector refuses with the reason read_only
the workspace is marked read-only in its index

criteria.title: Creating an item
given: An API that accepts POST /items and returns the identity 43 and the ETag W/"1"
criteria.when: the workspace creates an item
then: the connector returns the identity 43 and the revision W/"1"
item 43 appears in the next batch

criteria.title: Deletion with revision
given: Item 43 read with the revision W/"1"
criteria.when: the workspace deletes item 43 with that revision
then: the DELETE /items/43 request carries If-Match: W/"1"
a 412 answer is returned as stale_revision

criteria.title: Periodic polling
given: An interval of 60 seconds configured, and an item changed in the API after the last read
criteria.when: the interval expires
then: the connector reads the list again and emits a source-changed signal
the workspace index shows the item's new revision

criteria.title: Webhook
given: An API that calls the declared webhook when an item changes
criteria.when: the API calls the webhook for item 42
then: the connector emits the same source-changed signal as periodic polling

criteria.title: Unreachable API
given: An API that answers 503 with Retry-After: 30
criteria.when: the workspace asks for a batch
then: the connector reports source_unreachable with a delay of 30 seconds
no new request is sent before that delay
the index keeps its last window, dated

criteria.title: Timeout exceeded
given: A timeout of 5 seconds configured and an API that does not answer
criteria.when: the workspace asks for a batch
then: the request is aborted after 5 seconds
the connector reports source_unreachable with 5 seconds as the retry delay

criteria.title: Configuration checked with the definition
given: A workspace definition whose connector has a polling interval of -1
criteria.when: the agent checks the workspace
then: the check reports the invalid interval with its pointer and a correction

criteria.title: Connectors screen
given: Three workspaces plugged into three APIs, one of them unreachable since 9:15 with a 503 error
criteria.when: the owner opens the Connectors screen
then: he sees three rows with the kind, the workspace, the URL, the variable name, reachable or not, read-only or not, the last refresh and the last error
the unreachable row shows "no, since 09:15" and "503"

criteria.title: Connection test
given: A connector configured towards an API that answers 200 to the list
criteria.when: the owner clicks Test
then: the screen shows "reachable" with the date
no item is created, changed or deleted in the API

criteria.title: Failed connection test
given: A connector configured towards an API that answers 401
criteria.when: the owner clicks Test
then: the screen shows the 401 error and the environment variable to check

criteria.title: Indicator in the workspace
given: A workspace whose source has been unreachable since 9:15
criteria.when: the owner opens the workspace
then: the index shows the indicator "source unreachable since 09:15" without opening the Connectors screen
the indicator leads to the Connectors screen

criteria.title: Secret refused
given: An agent that passes the value s3cret in the connector definition
criteria.when: the agent checks or saves the definition
then: Maket refuses and asks for the name of an environment variable instead
the value s3cret is written nowhere

anchors.note: New factory next to createLocalItemSource: it implements ItemSource without changing it. capabilities() returns readOnly true, without create, put or delete, when the configuration declares neither an ETag nor a revision field; writing is then refused as read_only by sourceWrite.

list and get are synchronous in ItemSource: refresh calls the API (cursor listing and search, at most 500 items per batch, total when the API gives it; single item with its revision) and fills the memory that list and get then serve.
Sends PUT with If-Match carrying the expected revision; on 412, reads the item again and raises stale_revision with currentRevision and the current data.
Sends POST and returns the identity and revision assigned by the API, read at the declared JSON pointers.
Sends DELETE with If-Match carrying the expected revision; a 412 answer becomes stale_revision.
Converts the API's pagination (page number, Link header or next-cursor pointer) into the workspace's opaque cursor, encoded like the local source's one.

Only network call site: reads the secret from process.env under the configured name and sends it with every request without ever writing it; aborts the request at the configured timeout with an AbortSignal; returns source_unreachable with retryAfter on a network error, a 5xx or a timeout, without retrying.
Reads the list again at the configured interval, compares the revisions with the last read and emits structured-workspace:source-changed on the bus when one differs; stopped by close().

Optional route that receives the API's webhook calls and emits the same structured-workspace:source-changed as polling; mounted through ROUTER_NAMES in packages/server/src/routes/index.ts and registered in bootstrap.ts.

The registry opens createHttpItemSource when the definition declares an HTTP source, createLocalItemSource otherwise; it gains the state of each connector (reachable, read-only, last refresh, last error) and a connection test that performs a single list read without writing.

Adds source, of type StructuredWorkspaceHttpSource: base URL, name of the secret's environment variable, JSON pointers for the list, next cursor, identity and revision (ETag or field), polling interval, timeout. It is stored with the definition, with no repository change.

Adds the check of the source to the same check as the rest of the definition; a secret value (secret, token or password key, or header value) is refused with a correction that points to the name of the environment variable.
The zod schema of representation_schema accepts source, written by create and update_definition; the tool description says that only the name of the secret's variable is given there.

Returns to the agent stale_revision with the current revision and data, read_only with its reason, source_unreachable with the status, the API's message and the delay before a retry; today only request refusals are translated.
Passes expected_revision to deleteItem; expected_revision also accepts a text revision (ETag) for update_item and delete_item.
Passes the source's revision as is to put; staleItemRevision no longer converts currentRevision to a number and attaches the data read again after a 412.
Receives the expected revision and passes it to the source's delete, which sends it in If-Match.
Keeps source from the entered representation in the materialised definition, for create as for update_definition.
Attaches to each view the connector state read in ItemSources, broadcast by structured_workspaces_changed at every state change.
Adds sourceStatus: kind, base URL, variable name, reachable or unreachable since a date, read-only, last refresh, last error; never the secret's value.
New command test_connector and its result signal connector_test_result (reachable, or status, message and advised delay), added to the WorkspaceCommand and WorkspaceSignal unions.
Handles test_connector: calls the registry's connection test and answers the client; plugged into the switch of createWsHandler.
Connectors screen of wireframe ART-03: one row per source with kind, workspace, base URL, variable name, reachable, read-only, last refresh, last error and a Test button; no field to enter a secret.
Adds the connectors view to the library bar, next to structured-workspaces, which shows ConnectorsTab.
Sends test_connector for a workspace and stores the result received for the Connectors screen.

Indicator of wireframe ART-04 placed in CollectionDocument above the index search: reachable with the refresh date, unreachable since a date with the last error, or read-only, with a link to the Connectors screen.
French labels of the Connectors screen and of the indicator; the same keys in English in packages/client/src/i18n/en.json.
